title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 20 (Agreement void where both parties are under mistake as to matter of fact)

content.overview: Section 20 provides that where both the parties to an agreement are under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement, the agreement is void. An erroneous opinion as to the value of the thing which forms the subject-matter of the agreement is not to be deemed a mistake as to a matter of fact.
content.glance: Bilateral mistake of fact essential to the agreement → void; erroneous opinion as to value is not such a mistake.
content.study: Where both parties are under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement, the agreement is void. An erroneous opinion as to the value of the subject-matter is not a mistake as to a matter of fact. Unilateral mistake of fact does not by itself make a contract voidable (s. 22). Mistake of law is governed by s. 21. Current-law framing: identify the shared mistake; test whether it is as to a fact essential to the agreement; exclude mere value opinions; conclude voidness.

sections.heading: Bilateral mistake of essential fact
sections.body: Both parties under a mistake as to a matter of fact essential to the agreement — agreement void.

sections.heading: Value not a fact mistake
sections.body: Erroneous opinion as to the value of the subject-matter is not a mistake as to a matter of fact.

provisions.title: Agreement void where both parties are under mistake as to matter of fact

examples.title: Subject-matter already destroyed
examples.body: Both parties contract for a specific thing that, unknown to both, has already ceased to exist. The agreement is void under s. 20.

hypotheticals.question: Does a bad bargain void the agreement under s. 20?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Erroneous opinion as to value is not a mistake as to a matter of fact.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-20
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Any mistake by either party voids the contract.
misconceptions.correction: Section 20 requires both parties under a mistake as to an essential fact; unilateral mistake is under s. 22.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 20 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the shared mistake. II. Test essential fact. III. Exclude value opinions. IV. Conclude voidness.
